newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended higher, underpinned by gains in German Bunds, although volume was thin and shorter maturities lagged behind the long end.
German bonds rallied after a Bundesbank council member said that the economic situation in Germany was grave, and that monetary policy could not afford to ignore this.
In Switzerland, the Swiss National Bank, as expected, left its discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent.
The Swiss market is now looking ahead to a new federal bond issue next week, expected by the market to be two tranches, each for a maximum of one billion Swiss francs.

Swiss insurer Winterthur launched a subordinated convertible "hailed" as the first catastrophe-linked offering. It was raised to 399.5 million Swiss francs from a planned 300 million. The bond will omit coupon payments in a particular year if more than 6,000 vehicles insured by the firm are damaged in any one weather-related incident with a specified period. The bond, with a three-year maturity, drew interest from foreign-based investors. "We are busy calculating it. It has a certain attractiveness," said one foreign investor.
The bond was quoted by lead CSFB at par/100.50 compared with the par issue price.
Similar offerings have been done in yen, but the bond was believed to be the first of its type for the Swiss market.
Mar Conf futures up 20 bp at 117.11.
Mar Comi medium-term bond up five at 111.55
Mar Euro Swiss francs down three at 98.14.
